# Reference

<!-- Generated by docs/tools/reference.py from gen/claims.json, gen/kernels/, include/kairn/gen/bounds.hpp, proofs/gen/, results/milestone1/brute/ and docs/tools/reference_operations.py. Do not edit: run python3 docs/tools/reference.py. -->

Every public operation of Kairn, grouped by what it does, with the kernel that computes it, and the kernels that the public headers do not call yet. Each kernel has a page: its statement in plain mathematics, the C++ forms that reach it, what it requires, what is proved and with which theorem, its listing, and what the latest brute-force runs measured. [How to read a page](reading.md) explains each part.

Of the 63 kernels, 33 are proved and 30 are **UNVERIFIED**: [`add_2_1`](add_2_1.md), [`add_2_1_full`](add_2_1_full.md), [`add_2_2_full`](add_2_2_full.md), [`add_fast_2_2_full`](add_fast_2_2_full.md), [`ball_add_1`](ball_add_1.md), [`ball_add_1_full`](ball_add_1_full.md), [`ball_add_2`](ball_add_2.md), [`ball_add_2_full`](ball_add_2_full.md), [`ball_make_1`](ball_make_1.md), [`ball_make_2`](ball_make_2.md), [`ball_mul_1`](ball_mul_1.md), [`ball_mul_1_full`](ball_mul_1_full.md), [`ball_mul_2`](ball_mul_2.md), [`ball_mul_2_full`](ball_mul_2_full.md), [`ball_scale_1`](ball_scale_1.md), [`ball_scale_1_full`](ball_scale_1_full.md), [`ball_scale_2`](ball_scale_2.md), [`ball_scale_2_full`](ball_scale_2_full.md), [`ball_sub_1`](ball_sub_1.md), [`ball_sub_1_full`](ball_sub_1_full.md), [`ball_sub_2`](ball_sub_2.md), [`ball_sub_2_full`](ball_sub_2_full.md), [`make_2`](make_2.md), [`make_2_limbs`](make_2_limbs.md), [`mul_2_1_full`](mul_2_1_full.md), [`mul_2_2_full`](mul_2_2_full.md), [`mul_pow2_2_full`](mul_pow2_2_full.md), [`sub_1_2_full`](sub_1_2_full.md), [`sub_2_1_full`](sub_2_1_full.md), [`sub_2_2_full`](sub_2_2_full.md).

18 kernels have a statement on finite operands and one on infinite and NaN operands; the second is **UNVERIFIED** for all of them.

The operations that call an UNVERIFIED kernel need the marker `kairn::unverified` on an operand: those of [`add_2_1`](add_2_1.md), [`ball_add_1`](ball_add_1.md), [`ball_add_2`](ball_add_2.md), [`ball_mul_1`](ball_mul_1.md), [`ball_mul_2`](ball_mul_2.md), [`ball_scale_1`](ball_scale_1.md), [`ball_scale_2`](ball_scale_2.md), [`ball_sub_1`](ball_sub_1.md), [`ball_sub_2`](ball_sub_2.md).

Notation: $u = 2^{-p}$ is the unit roundoff of the limb type `T` ($2^{-53}$ for `double`, $2^{-24}$ for `float`), $\eta$ its smallest positive number, $\mathrm{RN}$ rounding to nearest with ties to even, and a two-limb number $x = x_0 + x_1$ is *normalized* when $x_0 = \mathrm{RN}(x_0 + x_1)$ ([Numbers](../developer/design/phase0/numbers.md#notation)). An operand of type `Expansion<T, 1>` next to an `Expansion<T, 2>` is converted to two limbs, exactly, and the two-limb form applies.

## Construction and access

Making numbers and balls, and reading their parts.

| C++ | Operands | What it gives | Kernel |
|---|---|---|---|
| not yet called by the public headers | - | $x = a$ exactly, canonical | [`make_2`](make_2.md) **UNVERIFIED** |
| not yet called by the public headers | - | $x = y$ exactly, canonical | [`make_2_limbs`](make_2_limbs.md) **UNVERIFIED** |
| not yet called by the public headers | - | the ball of center $c$ and radius $r$, canonical | [`ball_make_1`](ball_make_1.md) **UNVERIFIED** |
| not yet called by the public headers | - | the ball of center $c$ and radius $r$, canonical | [`ball_make_2`](ball_make_2.md) **UNVERIFIED** |
| `Expansion<T, K>()` | none | zero | none |
| `Expansion<T, 2>(a)` | `T` | the value $a$ exactly: $(a, 0)$, with a $-0$ made $+0$; for an infinite or NaN $a$, $(\pm\infty, 0)$ or $(\mathrm{NaN}, \mathrm{NaN})$ | none |
| `Expansion<T, 2>(a)` | `Expansion<T, 1>` | the value $a$ exactly: $(a, 0)$, with a $-0$ made $+0$; for an infinite or NaN $a$, $(\pm\infty, 0)$ or $(\mathrm{NaN}, \mathrm{NaN})$, where $a$ is the limb of the one-limb number | none |
| `Expansion<T, 1>(a)` | `T` | the value $a$ | none |
| `Expansion<T, K>::from_limbs(p)` | `const T*` | the number with these limbs, which must form a normalized number; checked when `KAIRN_CHECKS` is 1 | none |
| `Expansion<T, K>::from_limbs_unchecked(p)` | `const T*` | the same without the check: limbs that do not form a normalized number give results without any guarantee | none |
| `x.limb[i]` | `Expansion<T, K>` | the limbs, most significant first; a limb written directly must not be a product the compiler can see | none |
| `Ball<T, K>()` | none | the point 0: center 0, radius 0 | none |
| `Ball<T, K>(a)` | `T` | the point $a$: center $a$, radius 0 | none |
| `Ball<T, K>(c)` | `Expansion<T, K>` | the point $c$: center $c$, radius 0 | none |
| `Ball<T, K>(c, r)` | `Expansion<T, K>`, `T` | the ball of center $c$ and radius $r$; requires a normalized $c$ and $r \ge 0$, checked when `KAIRN_CHECKS` is 1 | none |
| `X.center()` | `Ball<T, K>` | the center | none |
| `X.radius()` | `Ball<T, K>` | the radius | none |
| `sign(x)` | `Expansion<T, K>` | $-1$, $0$ or $+1$, from the leading limb; $0$ for NaN | none |
| `isfinite(x)` | `Expansion<T, K>` | whether the leading limb is finite | none |
| `is_normalized(x)` | `Expansion<T, K>` | whether every limb is finite and, for two limbs, $x_0 + x_1$ rounds to $x_0$ | none |

| `a * b`, `a *= b` | `Expansion<T, 1>`, `Expansion<T, 1>` | $p = \mathrm{RN}(a b)$; $\lvert p - a b\rvert \le \frac{u}{1 + u}\,\lvert a b\rvert + \tfrac{1}{2}\,\eta$ | [`mul_1_1`](mul_1_1.md) |

## Comparisons

Whether one value is below, at most, or equal to another.

| C++ | Operands | What it gives | Kernel |
|---|---|---|---|
| `x < y`, `y > x` | `Expansion<T, 2>`, `Expansion<T, 2>` | exactly whether $x < y$ | [`lt_2_2`](lt_2_2.md) |
| `x <= y`, `y >= x` | `Expansion<T, 2>`, `Expansion<T, 2>` | exactly whether $x \le y$ | [`le_2_2`](le_2_2.md) |
| `x == y`, `x != y` | `Expansion<T, 2>`, `Expansion<T, 2>` | exactly whether $x = y$ | [`eq_2_2`](eq_2_2.md) |
| `x < a`, `a > x` | `Expansion<T, 2>`, `T` | exactly whether $x < a$ | [`lt_2_1`](lt_2_1.md) |
| `x <= a`, `a >= x` | `Expansion<T, 2>`, `T` | exactly whether $x \le a$ | [`le_2_1`](le_2_1.md) |
| `x == a`, `a == x`, `x != a`, `a != x` | `Expansion<T, 2>`, `T` | exactly whether $x = a$ | [`eq_2_1`](eq_2_1.md) |
| `a < y`, `y > a` | `T`, `Expansion<T, 2>` | exactly whether $a < y$ | [`lt_1_2`](lt_1_2.md) |
| `a <= y`, `y >= a` | `T`, `Expansion<T, 2>` | exactly whether $a \le y$ | [`le_1_2`](le_1_2.md) |
| `x < y, x > y, x <= y, x >= y, x == y, x != y` | `Expansion<T, 1>`, `Expansion<T, 1>` | the comparison of `T`: exact; false if an operand is NaN (true for `!=`) | none |
